newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans to privatise big steelmaker.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans to privatise big steelmaker.

text.p: The Ukrainian government plans to privatise OP Dnipropetrovsk Metalurhichny Zavod (DMZ), one of the country's biggest steel factories, the head of the company's privatisation department said late on Monday.
"We hope that the issue of shares in our factory will begin in January, right after the government approves a privatisation plan," Olexander Matviyenko told Reuters.
Matviyenko outlined a possible breakdown of stakes in the enterprise, but added that the State Property Fund privatisation agency would make a final decision on allocation of shares.

The government and a strategic investor could each take a 26 percent stake, while workers would take an equal share, and the balance would be sold on stock exchanges and in return for privatisation certificates issued to the population, he said.

The Fund has put DMZ's initial capital at 21.2 million hryvnias. It produced 672,000 tonnes of pig-iron, 586,000 tonnes of steel and 484,000 tonnes of rolled iron from January to October this year, chief accountant Lydiya Vatchenko said.
Any strategic investor would have to let the plant continue to function as a steel maker, and agree not to reduce the number of workers, currently at 8,500, Vatchenko said.
DMZ's managers say it needs $300 million for modernisation. It owes its workers about four million hryvnias in back wages.

DMZ is one of 208 enterprises which the government designated earlier this year as eligible for strategic investment. However, parliament resolved last month to freeze such privatisations until it established rules for the process.
